Shows normal-appearing epidermis, thickened dermal collagen with activated fibroblasts, and lymphocytic perivascular infiltration.
Ill-defined erythematoedematous plaques with induration symmetrically distributed on the distal two-thirds of the shins.
response.rationale: The timing after pembrolizumab-containing therapy, sclerotic indurated plaques, and biopsy showing thickened dermal collagen with activated fibroblasts and lymphocytic inflammation are most consistent with an immunotherapy-related scleroderma-like reaction, whereas pemetrexed cutaneous toxicity is less specific for this sclerodermoid histopathologic pattern.

rejected.why: Pemetrexed toxicity alone does not explain the scleroderma-like dermal collagen thickening and symmetric sclerotic plaques; the histopathologic and clinical pattern favors an immune checkpoint inhibitor-related adverse event.
